# Setup

**Before knitting:** put `AHSnpa11bp.csv` (person level) and `AHSnpa11bb.csv` (biomedical level)
in the same folder as this `.Rmd` file, or change `data_dir` below. In RStudio, use
*Session → Set Working Directory → To Source File Location*, then click **Knit**.

```{r packages}
pkgs <- c("dplyr", "tidyr", "ggplot2", "survey", "pROC", "car",
          "knitr", "cluster", "MASS", "rpart", "class", "splines")
missing_pkgs <- pkgs[!pkgs %in% rownames(installed.packages())]
if (length(missing_pkgs) > 0) install.packages(missing_pkgs)

library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(ggplot2); library(survey)
library(pROC); library(knitr); library(cluster)
# MASS, rpart, class, car and splines are called with pkg:: so they don't mask dplyr::select

data_dir <- "."          # folder containing the two CSV files
out_dir  <- "q2_outputs" # tables are also saved here as CSV for the report
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
set.seed(3888)
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))
```

## Helper functions

```{r helpers}
fmt_p <- function(p) ifelse(is.na(p), "", ifelse(p < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", p)))

# Readable labels for model terms
term_labels <- c(
  "vitd3Mild"                          = "Vit D mild deficiency, 30–49 nmol/L (ref: adequate ≥50)",
  "vitd3ModSevere"                     = "Vit D moderate/severe deficiency, <30 nmol/L (ref: adequate)",
  "vitd_defDeficient"                  = "Vit D deficient, <50 nmol/L (ref: adequate)",
  "diabetesDiabetes"                   = "Diabetes (HbA1c) (ref: no diabetes)",
  "vitd_defDeficient:diabetesDiabetes" = "Interaction: Vit D deficient × Diabetes (ratio of ORs)",
  "upf10"                              = "UPF proxy, per +10 % of energy",
  "age"                                = "Age, per year",
  "sexFemale"                          = "Female (ref: male)",
  "energy_MJ"                          = "Total energy, per MJ/day",
  "pa_hours"                           = "Physical activity, per hour/week",
  "smokerEx"                           = "Ex-smoker (ref: never)",
  "smokerCurrent"                      = "Current smoker (ref: never)"
)
lab <- function(x) ifelse(x %in% names(term_labels), term_labels[x], x)

# Exponentiated coefficients with Wald CIs.
# For svyglm the t distribution uses the design degrees of freedom.
tidy_or <- function(fit) {
  s  <- summary(fit)
  ct <- s$coefficients
  df <- if (inherits(fit, "svyglm")) s$df.residual else Inf
  crit <- qt(0.975, df)
  data.frame(term = rownames(ct),
             est  = exp(ct[, 1]),
             lo   = exp(ct[, 1] - crit * ct[, 2]),
             hi   = exp(ct[, 1] + crit * ct[, 2]),
             p    = ct[, 4], row.names = NULL)
}

# Table of ORs for several fitted models (one column per model)
or_compare <- function(fits) {
  rows <- lapply(names(fits), function(m) {
    tidy_or(fits[[m]]) %>% filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
      transmute(term, model = m,
                value = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f–%.2f); p=%s", est, lo, hi, fmt_p(p)))
  })
  bind_rows(rows) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = model, values_from = value, values_fill = "—") %>%
    mutate(term = lab(term)) %>% rename(Term = term)
}

# One-line summary of a single term, for use in the text
or_txt <- function(fit, term, what = "OR") {
  r <- tidy_or(fit) %>% filter(.data$term == !!term)
  sprintf("%s = %.2f (95%% CI %.2f–%.2f, p = %s)", what, r$est, r$lo, r$hi, fmt_p(r$p))
}
p_of   <- function(fit, term) tidy_or(fit) %>% filter(.data$term == !!term) %>% pull(p)
sigtxt <- function(p) ifelse(p < 0.05, "statistically significant", "not statistically significant")

# % change in the exposure OR when confounders are added (>10% = meaningful confounding)
pct_change <- function(crude, adj, term) {
  a <- tidy_or(crude) %>% filter(.data$term == !!term) %>% pull(est)
  b <- tidy_or(adj)   %>% filter(.data$term == !!term) %>% pull(est)
  100 * (b - a) / a
}

# Unweighted glm summaries used for AIC / likelihood-ratio tests / pseudo-R2
glm_fit <- function(f, data) glm(f, data = data, family = binomial)
# McFadden pseudo-R2 = 1 - logL(model)/logL(null); for 0/1 data this equals 1 - deviance/null deviance
mcfadden <- function(fit) 1 - fit$deviance / fit$null.deviance

brier <- function(y, p) mean((y - p)^2)
mk_roc <- function(y, p) pROC::roc(response = y, predictor = p,
                                   levels = c(0, 1), direction = "<", quiet = TRUE)

# Hosmer–Lemeshow goodness-of-fit test (implemented here so no extra package is needed)
hosmer_lemeshow <- function(y, p, g = 10) {
  br  <- unique(quantile(p, probs = seq(0, 1, length.out = g + 1)))
  grp <- cut(p, br, include.lowest = TRUE)
  obs <- tapply(y, grp, sum); expd <- tapply(p, grp, sum); n <- tapply(y, grp, length)
  stat <- sum((obs - expd)^2 / (expd * (1 - expd / n)))
  df <- length(n) - 2
  c(statistic = stat, df = df, p.value = pchisq(stat, df, lower.tail = FALSE))
}

# Adjusted Rand index between two labelings (cluster vs obesity)
adj_rand <- function(a, b) {
  tab <- table(a, b); n <- sum(tab)
  sc <- sum(choose(tab, 2)); sa <- sum(choose(rowSums(tab), 2)); sb <- sum(choose(colSums(tab), 2))
  expct <- sa * sb / choose(n, 2)
  (sc - expct) / ((sa + sb) / 2 - expct)
}

save_tab <- function(df, name) write.csv(df, file.path(out_dir, paste0(name, ".csv")), row.names = FALSE)
```

# Data preparation

## Read and merge

The person file and biomedical file share the selected-person identifier `ABSPID` (one row per person in each file).

```{r read}
bp_cols <- c("ABSHID", "ABSPID", "AGEC", "SEX", "FEMLSBC", "BMISC", "PHDCMWBC",
             "SATPER1", "PEADDSD1", "ENERGYT1", "EXLWTBC", "SMKSTAT", "NPAFINWT")
bb_cols <- c("ABSPID", "BIORESPC", "VDLCMRGT", "DIABPRVE", "NHMSPERW",
             sprintf("RPWGT%02d", 1:60))

bp <- read.csv(file.path(data_dir, "AHSnpa11bp.csv"))[, bp_cols]
bb <- read.csv(file.path(data_dir, "AHSnpa11bb.csv"))[, bb_cols]

stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(bp$ABSPID), !anyDuplicated(bb$ABSPID))
raw <- left_join(bp, bb, by = "ABSPID")
c(person_rows = nrow(bp), biomedical_rows = nrow(bb), merged = nrow(raw))
```

## Recode variables (codes from the NNPAS Basic CURF data item list)

| Variable | Source | Coding used |
|---|---|---|
| `obese` | `BMISC` | 1 if measured BMI ≥ 30; codes 0/98/99 (not applicable / not measured / not known) → missing |
| `vitd3` | `VDLCMRGT` | 1 Adequate ≥50 nmol/L, 2 Mild 30–49, 3 Moderate/severe <30; 0/8 → missing |
| `vitd_def` | `VDLCMRGT` | Deficient (<50 nmol/L) vs adequate — used for the interaction because cells are small |
| `diabetes` | `DIABPRVE` | Diabetes = 1 known or 2 newly diagnosed; No diabetes = 3 normal or 4 at risk; 0/8 → missing |
| `upf` | `SATPER1 + PEADDSD1` | % energy from saturated + trans fat + % energy from added sugars (Day 1); modelled per 10 %E |
| `age`, `sex` | `AGEC`, `SEX` | Confounders |
| Restriction | `AGEC`, `FEMLSBC` | Age 18–64; currently pregnant women (`FEMLSBC` = 2) excluded |
| Sensitivity only | `PHDCMWBC`, `ENERGYT1`, `EXLWTBC`, `SMKSTAT` | Waist-based obesity, energy, physical activity, smoking |

```{r recode}
dat <- raw %>%
  filter(AGEC >= 18, AGEC <= 64, FEMLSBC != 2) %>%
  mutate(
    BMI      = ifelse(BMISC > 0 & BMISC < 97, BMISC, NA),
    obese    = as.integer(BMI >= 30),
    obese_f  = factor(obese, 0:1, c("Not obese", "Obese")),
    age      = AGEC,
    sex      = factor(SEX, 1:2, c("Male", "Female")),
    vitd_score = ifelse(VDLCMRGT %in% 1:3, VDLCMRGT, NA),       # 1 adequate … 3 mod/severe
    vitd3    = factor(vitd_score, 1:3, c("Adequate", "Mild", "ModSevere")),
    vitd_def = factor(ifelse(is.na(vitd_score), NA, as.integer(vitd_score >= 2)),
                      0:1, c("Adequate", "Deficient")),
    diabetes = factor(ifelse(DIABPRVE %in% 1:4, as.integer(DIABPRVE <= 2), NA),
                      0:1, c("No diabetes", "Diabetes")),
    upf      = SATPER1 + PEADDSD1,
    upf10    = upf / 10,
    waist    = ifelse(PHDCMWBC > 0 & PHDCMWBC < 998, PHDCMWBC, NA),
    waist_obese = as.integer((sex == "Male" & waist >= 94) | (sex == "Female" & waist >= 80)),
    energy_MJ = ENERGYT1 / 1000,
    pa_hours  = ifelse(EXLWTBC <= 2100, EXLWTBC / 60, NA),        # 9996/9999 → missing
    smoker    = factor(case_when(SMKSTAT %in% 1:3 ~ "Current", SMKSTAT == 4 ~ "Ex",
                                 SMKSTAT == 5 ~ "Never"), levels = c("Never", "Ex", "Current"))
  )

# Analysis samples (complete cases)
d_full <- dat %>% filter(!is.na(obese), !is.na(upf))                       # UPF analysis (Person 2)
d_bio  <- d_full %>% filter(!is.na(vitd3), !is.na(diabetes), NHMSPERW > 0)  # Vit D analyses (Persons 1, 3, 4 & Week 10)

sample_flow <- data.frame(
  Step = c("Merged NNPAS records", "Aged 18–64 and not pregnant",
           "+ valid measured BMI and UPF proxy (Person 2 sample)",
           "+ valid vitamin D and HbA1c diabetes status (Persons 1, 3, 4; Week 10)"),
  n = c(nrow(raw), nrow(dat), nrow(d_full), nrow(d_bio)))
kable(sample_flow, caption = "Sample flow")
```

> Persons 1, 3 and 4 all use the **same** biomedical sample (n = `r nrow(d_bio)`), so their models are nested
> and can be compared directly with likelihood-ratio tests and AIC. Person 2 is fitted in the larger
> full sample (n = `r nrow(d_full)`) and re-fitted in the biomedical sample for comparison with Person 3.

## Survey designs

Population estimates use the ABS weights. The biomedical file supplies 60 delete-a-group jackknife replicate
weights (`RPWGT01–60`), which give design-based standard errors. The person file has no replicate weights, so the
full-sample design uses the person weight only.

```{r designs}
des_full <- svydesign(ids = ~1, weights = ~NPAFINWT, data = d_full)
des_bio  <- svrepdesign(data = d_bio, weights = ~NHMSPERW,
                        repweights = "RPWGT[0-9]+", type = "JK1",
                        scale = 59 / 60, mse = TRUE)
```

## Descriptive overview

```{r descriptives}
prev_by <- function(var, design) {
  r <- svyby(~obese, as.formula(paste0("~", var)), design, svymean, na.rm = TRUE)
  n <- table(design$variables[[var]])
  data.frame(Variable = var, Group = as.character(r[[var]]),
             n = as.integer(n[as.character(r[[var]])]),
             `Weighted obesity %` = sprintf("%.1f (SE %.1f)", 100 * r$obese, 100 * SE(r)),
             check.names = FALSE)
}
d_bio$upf_q  <- cut(d_bio$upf,  quantile(d_bio$upf,  0:4 / 4), include.lowest = TRUE, labels = paste0("Q", 1:4))
d_full$upf_q <- cut(d_full$upf, quantile(d_full$upf, 0:4 / 4), include.lowest = TRUE, labels = paste0("Q", 1:4))
des_bio  <- update(des_bio,  upf_q = d_bio$upf_q)
des_full <- update(des_full, upf_q = d_full$upf_q)

desc_tab <- bind_rows(prev_by("vitd3", des_bio), prev_by("diabetes", des_bio),
                      prev_by("sex", des_bio), prev_by("upf_q", des_full))
kable(desc_tab, caption = "Survey-weighted obesity prevalence by group (unadjusted)")
save_tab(desc_tab, "table1_weighted_prevalence")

kable(table(VitaminD = d_bio$vitd3, Diabetes = d_bio$diabetes),
      caption = "Cell counts: vitamin D × diabetes (why the interaction uses binary deficiency)")
```

```{r eda-plot, fig.height=4}
ggplot(d_full, aes(upf, BMI)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.15, size = 0.8) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = TRUE, colour = "firebrick") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 30, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = "UPF proxy (% energy from sat/trans fat + added sugar)", y = "Measured BMI",
       title = "BMI against the UPF proxy (dashed line = obesity threshold)")
```

# Week 9 – Model building and significance of the independent variables

All models are logistic regressions for `logit P(Obese = 1)`. For each person we report:

* **Survey-weighted ORs** (`svyglm`, quasibinomial, replicate-weight SEs) — the primary, population-level result;
* the **joint Wald test** for multi-level factors (`regTermTest`);
* **unweighted `glm` likelihood-ratio tests and AIC**, used for model comparison;
* the **% change in the exposure OR** after adjustment (a change of more than 10% suggests confounding by age/sex).

```{r fit-all}
f <- list(
  P1_crude = obese ~ vitd3,
  P1_adj   = obese ~ vitd3 + age + sex,
  P2_crude = obese ~ upf10,
  P2_adj   = obese ~ upf10 + age + sex,
  P3_crude = obese ~ vitd3 + upf10,
  P3_adj   = obese ~ vitd3 + upf10 + age + sex,
  P4_main  = obese ~ vitd_def + diabetes + upf10 + age + sex,
  P4_int   = obese ~ vitd_def * diabetes + upf10 + age + sex   # = the full model in the brief
)

# Survey-weighted fits (biomedical design for everything except Person 2 primary)
sw <- lapply(f, function(ff) svyglm(ff, design = des_bio, family = quasibinomial()))
sw$P2_crude_full <- svyglm(f$P2_crude, design = des_full, family = quasibinomial())
sw$P2_adj_full   <- svyglm(f$P2_adj,   design = des_full, family = quasibinomial())

# Unweighted fits (same biomedical sample) for LRT / AIC
uw <- lapply(f, glm_fit, data = d_bio)
uw$P2_crude_full <- glm_fit(f$P2_crude, d_full)
uw$P2_adj_full   <- glm_fit(f$P2_adj,   d_full)
```

## Person 1 – Obesity ~ Vitamin D

```{r p1}
kable(or_compare(list(`Crude (weighted)` = sw$P1_crude, `Adjusted (weighted)` = sw$P1_adj,
                      `Adjusted (unweighted)` = uw$P1_adj)),
      caption = "Person 1: odds ratios (95% CI); p")

p1_joint_c <- regTermTest(sw$P1_crude, ~vitd3)
p1_joint_a <- regTermTest(sw$P1_adj,   ~vitd3)
p1_lrt     <- drop1(uw$P1_adj, test = "LRT")
kable(data.frame(Test = c("Joint Wald F, vitamin D (crude, weighted)",
                          "Joint Wald F, vitamin D (adjusted, weighted)",
                          "Likelihood-ratio χ², vitamin D (adjusted, unweighted)"),
                 p = fmt_p(c(p1_joint_c$p, p1_joint_a$p, p1_lrt["vitd3", "Pr(>Chi)"]))),
      caption = "Overall significance of vitamin D (2 df)")
```

**Interpretation (auto-filled).** After adjusting for age and sex, moderate/severe deficiency had
`r or_txt(sw$P1_adj, "vitd3ModSevere")` and mild deficiency had `r or_txt(sw$P1_adj, "vitd3Mild")` compared
with adequate vitamin D. The overall vitamin D effect was `r sigtxt(p1_joint_a$p)` (joint p = `r fmt_p(p1_joint_a$p)`).
Adjustment changed the moderate/severe OR by `r sprintf("%.1f", pct_change(sw$P1_crude, sw$P1_adj, "vitd3ModSevere"))`%
and the mild OR by `r sprintf("%.1f", pct_change(sw$P1_crude, sw$P1_adj, "vitd3Mild"))`%.

*Discussion prompts:* direction of the association (lower vitamin D ↔ higher odds of obesity is consistent with
vitamin D being sequestered in adipose tissue, i.e. obesity may cause low vitamin D rather than the reverse);
the cross-sectional design cannot establish causality; the season of the blood test is not adjusted for.

## Person 2 – Obesity ~ UPF proxy

```{r p2}
kable(or_compare(list(`Crude, full sample` = sw$P2_crude_full, `Adjusted, full sample` = sw$P2_adj_full,
                      `Crude, biomedical sample` = sw$P2_crude, `Adjusted, biomedical sample` = sw$P2_adj)),
      caption = "Person 2: odds ratios per +10 % energy from the UPF proxy (weighted)")
p2_lrt <- drop1(uw$P2_adj_full, test = "LRT")
```

**Interpretation (auto-filled).** In the full sample (n = `r nrow(d_full)`), each additional 10 % of energy from
saturated/trans fat plus added sugar had `r or_txt(sw$P2_adj_full, "upf10")` after adjusting for age and sex
(likelihood-ratio p = `r fmt_p(p2_lrt["upf10", "Pr(>Chi)"])`), which is `r sigtxt(p_of(sw$P2_adj_full, "upf10"))`.
Adjustment changed the OR by `r sprintf("%.1f", pct_change(sw$P2_crude_full, sw$P2_adj_full, "upf10"))`%.

*Discussion prompts:* the proxy comes from a single 24-hour recall, so day-to-day variation dilutes the association
towards OR = 1; people with obesity may under-report energy-dense foods (reporting bias); the proxy measures
nutrients, not processing level (NOVA), so it is only an indirect UPF marker.

## Person 3 – Obesity ~ Vitamin D + UPF

```{r p3}
kable(or_compare(list(`Vit D only (adj.)` = sw$P1_adj, `UPF only (adj.)` = sw$P2_adj,
                      `Both, crude` = sw$P3_crude, `Both, adjusted` = sw$P3_adj)),
      caption = "Person 3: mutual adjustment (all in the biomedical sample, weighted)")

p3_joint <- regTermTest(sw$P3_adj, ~vitd3)
p3_lrt   <- drop1(uw$P3_adj, test = "LRT")
kable(data.frame(Term = c("Vitamin D (2 df)", "UPF proxy (1 df)"),
                 `LRT p (unweighted)` = fmt_p(p3_lrt[c("vitd3", "upf10"), "Pr(>Chi)"]),
                 `Wald p (weighted)`  = fmt_p(c(p3_joint$p, p_of(sw$P3_adj, "upf10"))),
                 check.names = FALSE),
      caption = "Significance of each exposure in the mutually adjusted model")

# Are the two exposures related? (if not, mutual adjustment should change little)
upf_by_vitd <- svyby(~upf, ~vitd3, des_bio, svymean)
kable(data.frame(`Vitamin D` = upf_by_vitd$vitd3, `Weighted mean UPF %E` = round(upf_by_vitd$upf, 1),
                 SE = round(SE(upf_by_vitd), 2), check.names = FALSE),
      caption = sprintf("UPF proxy by vitamin D group (design-based Wald test p = %s)",
                        fmt_p(regTermTest(svyglm(upf ~ vitd3, des_bio), ~vitd3)$p)))
kable(round(car::vif(uw$P3_adj), 2), caption = "Generalised VIF (values < 2 indicate no collinearity problem)")
```

**Interpretation (auto-filled).** With both exposures in the model, moderate/severe vitamin D deficiency had
`r or_txt(sw$P3_adj, "vitd3ModSevere")` and the UPF proxy had `r or_txt(sw$P3_adj, "upf10")`.
Compared with the single-exposure models, the vitamin D OR changed by
`r sprintf("%.1f", pct_change(sw$P1_adj, sw$P3_adj, "vitd3ModSevere"))`% and the UPF OR by
`r sprintf("%.1f", pct_change(sw$P2_adj, sw$P3_adj, "upf10"))`%, i.e. the two exposures act largely
`r ifelse(abs(pct_change(sw$P1_adj, sw$P3_adj, "vitd3ModSevere")) < 10 & abs(pct_change(sw$P2_adj, sw$P3_adj, "upf10")) < 10, "independently", "non-independently (they share part of their association)")`.

*Discussion prompts (bigger discussion):* compare the UPF OR in the full vs biomedical sample (precision is lost in the
smaller sample, and blood-test participants may differ from non-participants); whether diet is on the causal path to
low vitamin D (if so, adjusting for it would be over-adjustment); residual confounding by physical activity, sun
exposure and socioeconomic status (see Sensitivity analyses).

## Person 4 – Interaction of diabetes and vitamin D on obesity

Full model from the brief:
$\text{logit}\,P(\text{Obese}) = \beta_0 + \beta_1\text{VitD} + \beta_2\text{Diabetes} + \beta_3(\text{VitD}\times\text{Diabetes}) + \beta_4\text{UPF} + \beta_5\text{Age} + \beta_6\text{Sex}$.
Vitamin D is used as *deficient vs adequate* because only `r sum(d_bio$diabetes == "Diabetes" & d_bio$vitd3 == "ModSevere")`
people with diabetes have moderate/severe deficiency.

```{r p4}
kable(or_compare(list(`Main effects` = sw$P4_main, `With interaction` = sw$P4_int)),
      caption = "Person 4: weighted odds ratios")

int_term <- "vitd_defDeficient:diabetesDiabetes"
p4_wald  <- regTermTest(sw$P4_int, ~vitd_def:diabetes)
p4_lrt   <- anova(uw$P4_main, uw$P4_int, test = "LRT")

# Stratum-specific ORs for vitamin D deficiency
strat <- svycontrast(sw$P4_int, list(
  `No diabetes` = c("vitd_defDeficient" = 1),
  `Diabetes`    = c("vitd_defDeficient" = 1, "vitd_defDeficient:diabetesDiabetes" = 1)))
ddf <- summary(sw$P4_int)$df.residual
strat_tab <- data.frame(Group = names(coef(strat)), n = as.integer(table(d_bio$diabetes)),
                        `OR for Vit D deficiency` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f–%.2f)",
                          exp(coef(strat)), exp(coef(strat) - qt(.975, ddf) * SE(strat)),
                          exp(coef(strat) + qt(.975, ddf) * SE(strat))),
                        p = fmt_p(2 * pt(-abs(coef(strat) / SE(strat)), ddf)),
                        check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
kable(strat_tab, caption = "Effect of vitamin D deficiency within each diabetes group")

kable(data.frame(Test = c("Wald F for interaction (weighted)", "LRT main vs interaction (unweighted)"),
                 p = fmt_p(c(p4_wald$p, p4_lrt$`Pr(>Chi)`[2]))),
      caption = "Is the vitamin D–obesity association different by diabetes status?")
```

```{r p4-standardised, fig.height=4}
# Age/sex/UPF-standardised obesity prevalence for each Vit D × diabetes combination,
# with jackknife SEs from the 60 replicate weights.
combos <- expand.grid(vitd_def = levels(d_bio$vitd_def), diabetes = levels(d_bio$diabetes))
std_prev <- withReplicates(des_bio, function(w, data) {
  data$rep_w <- w / mean(w)            # rescale to mean 1 (as svyglm does) so IRLS converges
  fit <- glm(f$P4_int, data = data, weights = rep_w, family = quasibinomial())
  sapply(seq_len(nrow(combos)), function(i) {
    nd <- data; nd$vitd_def <- combos$vitd_def[i]; nd$diabetes <- combos$diabetes[i]
    nd$vitd_def <- factor(nd$vitd_def, levels(d_bio$vitd_def))
    nd$diabetes <- factor(nd$diabetes, levels(d_bio$diabetes))
    weighted.mean(predict(fit, nd, type = "response"), w)
  })
})
combos$prev <- as.numeric(coef(std_prev)); combos$se <- as.numeric(SE(std_prev))

ggplot(combos, aes(vitd_def, 100 * prev, colour = diabetes, group = diabetes)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, position = position_dodge(0.3)) +
  geom_line(position = position_dodge(0.3)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = 100 * (prev - 1.96 * se), ymax = 100 * (prev + 1.96 * se)),
                width = 0.15, position = position_dodge(0.3)) +
  labs(x = "Vitamin D status", y = "Standardised obesity prevalence (%)", colour = NULL,
       title = "Model-standardised obesity prevalence (full interaction model)",
       subtitle = "Non-parallel lines suggest interaction, but check the wide CIs in the diabetes group")
```

**Interpretation (auto-filled).** The interaction term was `r or_txt(sw$P4_int, int_term, "ratio of ORs")`;
the LRT comparing models with and without the interaction gave p = `r fmt_p(p4_lrt[["Pr(>Chi)"]][2])`.
This is `r sigtxt(p4_wald$p)`, so we `r ifelse(p4_wald$p < 0.05, "have", "do not have")` evidence that
the vitamin D–obesity association differs between people with and without diabetes. Only
`r sum(d_bio$diabetes == "Diabetes")` participants have diabetes, so the test has low power and the
diabetic-group estimate is imprecise.

```{r w9-compare}
cmp_names <- c("P1_crude", "P1_adj", "P2_crude", "P2_adj", "P3_crude", "P3_adj", "P4_main", "P4_int")
w9 <- data.frame(Model = cmp_names,
                 Formula = sapply(f[cmp_names], function(x) deparse(x[[3]])),
                 n = sapply(uw[cmp_names], nobs),
                 AIC = round(sapply(uw[cmp_names], AIC), 1),
                 `McFadden R2` = round(sapply(uw[cmp_names], mcfadden), 3), check.names = FALSE)
w9$`ΔAIC vs best` <- round(w9$AIC - min(w9$AIC), 1)

# Nested likelihood-ratio tests along the model-building path

               c("P2_adj", "P3_adj"), c("P4_main", "P4_int"))

lrt_tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(nested, function(m) {
  a <- anova(uw[[m[1]]], uw[[m[2]]], test = "LRT")
  data.frame(Comparison = paste(m[1], "→", m[2]), df = a$Df[2],
             `LR χ²` = round(a$Deviance[2], 2), p = fmt_p(a$`Pr(>Chi)`[2]), check.names = FALSE)
}))

# Combined weighted OR table for the report

                          P3_adj = sw$P3_adj, P4_int = sw$P4_int))
save_tab(all_or, "week9_adjusted_odds_ratios")
```

## Sensitivity analyses

1. **Prevalence ratios** (modified Poisson, log link, robust/replicate SEs) as planned in the proposal — ORs
   exaggerate risk ratios when the outcome is common (~27% here).
2. **Extended confounders**: + total energy, physical activity and smoking.
3. **Alternative outcome**: waist-circumference obesity (≥94 cm men, ≥80 cm women).

```{r sensitivity}
key_terms <- c("vitd3Mild", "vitd3ModSevere", "upf10", "vitd_defDeficient",
               "diabetesDiabetes", int_term)
pull_terms <- function(fit, spec, measure) tidy_or(fit) %>% filter(term %in% key_terms) %>%
  transmute(Specification = spec, Measure = measure, Term = lab(term),
            Term = sub("ratio of ORs", paste0("ratio of ", measure, "s"), Term),
            Estimate = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f–%.2f)", est, lo, hi), p = fmt_p(p),
            unstable = hi / lo > 1000)   # flags terms that are not estimable

start_vals <- function(ff, data) c(log(mean(data$obese)), rep(0, ncol(model.matrix(ff, data)) - 1))
des_pa    <- subset(des_bio, !is.na(pa_hours) & !is.na(smoker))
des_waist <- subset(des_bio, !is.na(waist_obese))
f_ext3 <- update(f$P3_adj, . ~ . + energy_MJ + pa_hours + smoker)
f_ext4 <- update(f$P4_int, . ~ . + energy_MJ + pa_hours + smoker)

sens <- bind_rows(
  pull_terms(sw$P3_adj, "Main: P3 adjusted", "OR"),
  pull_terms(sw$P4_int, "Main: P4 interaction", "OR"),
  pull_terms(svyglm(f$P3_adj, des_bio, family = quasipoisson(link = "log"),
                    start = start_vals(f$P3_adj, d_bio)), "Modified Poisson: P3", "PR"),
  pull_terms(svyglm(f$P4_int, des_bio, family = quasipoisson(link = "log"),
                    start = start_vals(f$P4_int, d_bio)), "Modified Poisson: P4", "PR"),
  pull_terms(svyglm(f_ext3, des_pa, family = quasibinomial()), "Extended confounders: P3", "OR"),
  pull_terms(svyglm(f_ext4, des_pa, family = quasibinomial()), "Extended confounders: P4", "OR"),
  pull_terms(svyglm(update(f$P3_adj, waist_obese ~ .), des_waist, family = quasibinomial()),
             "Waist outcome: P3", "OR"),
  pull_terms(svyglm(update(f$P4_int, waist_obese ~ .), des_waist, family = quasibinomial()),
             "Waist outcome: P4", "OR"))
kable(sens %>% select(-unstable), caption = "Key estimates under alternative specifications (survey-weighted)")
save_tab(sens, "week9_sensitivity")
waist_cells <- with(subset(d_bio, !is.na(waist_obese)),
                    table(VitD = vitd_def, Diabetes = diabetes, `Waist obese` = waist_obese))
```

`r if (any(sens$unstable)) paste0("**Note:** the following estimate(s) have extremely wide CIs and should be reported as *not estimable*: ", paste(paste0(sens$Specification[sens$unstable], " – ", sens$Term[sens$unstable]), collapse = "; "), ". For the waist outcome this is quasi-complete separation: almost everyone with diabetes meets the waist threshold (only ", waist_cells["Deficient", "Diabetes", "0"], " vitamin D-deficient participant(s) with diabetes are below it).") else ""`

# Week 10 – Testing the prediction of the models

Prediction is assessed on the common biomedical sample (n = `r nrow(d_bio)`) with unweighted models, because the
question is how well each model classifies *individuals*.

* **Hold-out test:** stratified 70/30 train/test split; models are fitted on the training set and scored on the test set.
* **Repeated 10-fold cross-validation** (5 repeats) gives a more stable estimate of out-of-sample AUC and Brier score.
* **Metrics:** AUC (discrimination, DeLong 95% CI), Brier score (overall accuracy of probabilities), sensitivity,
  specificity, PPV, NPV and accuracy. The classification threshold is chosen on the *training* data
  (Youden index) to avoid leakage. Calibration is checked with the Hosmer–Lemeshow test and a calibration plot.
* **Other methods:** LDA, a classification tree and k-nearest neighbours, plus **K-means** clustering (unsupervised).

```{r split}
d_pred <- d_bio
idx_train <- unlist(lapply(split(seq_len(nrow(d_pred)), d_pred$obese),
                           function(i) sample(i, round(0.7 * length(i)))))
train <- d_pred[idx_train, ]; test <- d_pred[-idx_train, ]
kable(data.frame(Set = c("Train", "Test"), n = c(nrow(train), nrow(test)),
                 `Obese %` = round(100 * c(mean(train$obese), mean(test$obese)), 1), check.names = FALSE),
      caption = "Stratified 70/30 split")

f_pred <- c(list(M0_AgeSex = obese ~ age + sex), f[cmp_names])
```

## Hold-out test-set performance

```{r holdout}
eval_model <- function(ff, name) {
  fit   <- glm(ff, data = train, family = binomial)
  p_tr  <- predict(fit, train, type = "response")
  p_te  <- predict(fit, test,  type = "response")
  thr   <- pROC::coords(mk_roc(train$obese, p_tr), "best", best.method = "youden",
                        ret = "threshold", transpose = FALSE)$threshold[1]
  r     <- mk_roc(test$obese, p_te); ci <- pROC::ci.auc(r)
  pred  <- as.integer(p_te >= thr); y <- test$obese
  tp <- sum(pred == 1 & y == 1); tn <- sum(pred == 0 & y == 0)
  fp <- sum(pred == 1 & y == 0); fn <- sum(pred == 0 & y == 1)
  list(roc = r, p = p_te,
       row = data.frame(Model = name,
                        AUC = sprintf("%.3f (%.3f–%.3f)", ci[2], ci[1], ci[3]), AUC_num = ci[2],
                        Brier = round(brier(y, p_te), 4), Threshold = round(thr, 3),
                        Sensitivity = round(tp / (tp + fn), 3), Specificity = round(tn / (tn + fp), 3),
                        PPV = round(tp / max(tp + fp, 1), 3), NPV = round(tn / max(tn + fn, 1), 3),
                        Accuracy = round((tp + tn) / length(y), 3),
                        `Accuracy @0.5` = round(mean(as.integer(p_te >= 0.5) == y), 3),
                        check.names = FALSE))
}
ho <- lapply(names(f_pred), function(m) eval_model(f_pred[[m]], m)); names(ho) <- names(f_pred)
ho_tab <- bind_rows(lapply(ho, `[[`, "row"))
kable(ho_tab %>% select(-AUC_num), caption = sprintf(
  "Test-set performance (no-information accuracy = %.3f, i.e. always predicting 'not obese')",
  1 - mean(test$obese)))
save_tab(ho_tab, "week10_holdout_performance")
```

```{r roc-plot, fig.height=5.5}
sel <- c("M0_AgeSex", "P1_adj", "P2_adj", "P3_adj", "P4_int")
pROC::ggroc(lapply(ho[sel], `[[`, "roc"), legacy.axes = TRUE) +
  geom_abline(linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  labs(title = "ROC curves on the test set", colour = "Model",
       x = "1 – Specificity", y = "Sensitivity")
```

```{r delong}
delong <- do.call(rbind, lapply(setdiff(names(ho), "M0_AgeSex"), function(m) {
  t <- pROC::roc.test(ho$M0_AgeSex$roc, ho[[m]]$roc, method = "delong", paired = TRUE)
  data.frame(Comparison = paste(m, "vs M0_AgeSex"),
             `ΔAUC` = round(as.numeric(pROC::auc(ho[[m]]$roc) - pROC::auc(ho$M0_AgeSex$roc)), 3),
             p = fmt_p(t$p.value), check.names = FALSE)
}))
t34 <- pROC::roc.test(ho$P3_adj$roc, ho$P4_int$roc, method = "delong", paired = TRUE)
delong <- rbind(delong, data.frame(Comparison = "P4_int vs P3_adj",
  `ΔAUC` = round(as.numeric(pROC::auc(ho$P4_int$roc) - pROC::auc(ho$P3_adj$roc)), 3),
  p = fmt_p(t34$p.value), check.names = FALSE))
kable(delong, caption = "DeLong tests: do the exposures improve discrimination beyond age and sex?")
```

## Repeated 10-fold cross-validation

```{r cv}
K <- 10; R <- 5
cv_res <- list()
for (r in seq_len(R)) {
  folds <- integer(nrow(d_pred))
  for (cls in 0:1) {                                   # stratified fold assignment
    ii <- which(d_pred$obese == cls)
    folds[ii] <- sample(rep(seq_len(K), length.out = length(ii)))
  }
  for (k in seq_len(K)) {
    tr <- d_pred[folds != k, ]; te <- d_pred[folds == k, ]
    for (m in names(f_pred)) {
      fit <- glm(f_pred[[m]], data = tr, family = binomial)
      p   <- predict(fit, te, type = "response")
      cv_res[[length(cv_res) + 1]] <- data.frame(model = m, rep = r, fold = k,
        auc = as.numeric(pROC::auc(mk_roc(te$obese, p))), brier = brier(te$obese, p))
    }
  }
}
cv_sum <- bind_rows(cv_res) %>% group_by(Model = model) %>%
  summarise(`CV AUC mean` = round(mean(auc), 3), `CV AUC SD` = round(sd(auc), 3),
            `CV Brier mean` = round(mean(brier), 4), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(`CV AUC mean`))
kable(cv_sum, caption = sprintf("%d × %d-fold cross-validation (null-model Brier = %.4f)",
                                R, K, mean(d_pred$obese) * (1 - mean(d_pred$obese))))
save_tab(cv_sum, "week10_cross_validation")

ggplot(bind_rows(cv_res), aes(reorder(model, auc), auc)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.4) + coord_flip() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "AUC per fold", title = "Cross-validated AUC across 50 folds")
```

## Calibration of the full model (P4_int)

```{r calibration, fig.height=4.5}
p_full <- ho$P4_int$p
hl <- hosmer_lemeshow(test$obese, p_full)
cal_fit <- glm(test$obese ~ qlogis(p_full), family = binomial)
cal_int <- glm(test$obese ~ offset(qlogis(p_full)), family = binomial)
kable(data.frame(Statistic = c("Hosmer–Lemeshow χ²", "HL df", "HL p-value",
                               "Calibration slope (ideal 1)", "Calibration-in-the-large (ideal 0)"),
                 Value = unname(c(round(hl[1], 2), hl[2], fmt_p(hl[3]),
                                  round(coef(cal_fit)[2], 3), round(coef(cal_int)[1], 3)))),
      caption = "Calibration on the test set")

cal_df <- data.frame(y = test$obese, p = p_full) %>%
  mutate(bin = ntile(p, 10)) %>% group_by(bin) %>%
  summarise(pred = mean(p), obs = mean(y), n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(se = sqrt(obs * (1 - obs) / n))
ggplot(cal_df, aes(pred, obs)) +
  geom_abline(linetype = "dashed") + geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = pmax(obs - 1.96 * se, 0), ymax = pmin(obs + 1.96 * se, 1)), width = 0.005) +
  coord_equal(xlim = c(0, 0.6), ylim = c(0, 0.6)) +
  labs(x = "Mean predicted probability (decile)", y = "Observed proportion obese",
       title = "Calibration plot – full interaction model (test set)")
```

## Comparison with other classification methods

Same predictors as the full model (Vit D deficiency, diabetes, UPF, age, sex). The tree uses equal priors so it does not
collapse to "everyone not obese"; the kNN `k` is tuned by leave-one-out CV on the training set.

```{r other-methods}
xvars <- function(d) data.frame(age = d$age, upf = d$upf,
                                vitd_def = as.integer(d$vitd_def == "Deficient"),
                                diabetes = as.integer(d$diabetes == "Diabetes"),
                                female = as.integer(d$sex == "Female"))
Xtr <- xvars(train); Xte <- xvars(test)
mu <- colMeans(Xtr); sdv <- apply(Xtr, 2, sd)
Ztr <- scale(Xtr, mu, sdv); Zte <- scale(Xte, mu, sdv)
f_x <- obese_f ~ vitd_def + diabetes + upf10 + age + sex

# Linear discriminant analysis
lda_fit <- MASS::lda(f_x, data = train)
p_lda   <- predict(lda_fit, test)$posterior[, "Obese"]

# Classification tree, pruned at the CV-optimal complexity
tree <- rpart::rpart(f_x, data = train, method = "class", parms = list(prior = c(0.5, 0.5)),
                     control = rpart::rpart.control(cp = 0.001, xval = 10, minbucket = 20))
best_cp <- tree$cptable[which.min(tree$cptable[, "xerror"]), "CP"]
tree_p  <- rpart::prune(tree, cp = best_cp)
p_tree  <- predict(tree_p, test, type = "prob")[, "Obese"]

# k-nearest neighbours, k tuned by LOOCV AUC on the training data
knn_prob <- function(pred) ifelse(pred == "1", attr(pred, "prob"), 1 - attr(pred, "prob"))
k_grid <- seq(5, 95, by = 10)
k_auc  <- sapply(k_grid, function(k) as.numeric(pROC::auc(mk_roc(train$obese,
            knn_prob(class::knn.cv(Ztr, factor(train$obese), k = k, prob = TRUE))))))
k_best <- k_grid[which.max(k_auc)]
p_knn  <- knn_prob(class::knn(Ztr, Zte, factor(train$obese), k = k_best, prob = TRUE))

methods <- list(ho$P4_int$p, p_lda, p_tree, p_knn)
names(methods) <- c("Logistic (P4_int)", "LDA", "Classification tree", paste0("kNN (k=", k_best, ")"))
meth_tab <- bind_rows(lapply(names(methods), function(m) {
  r <- mk_roc(test$obese, methods[[m]]); ci <- pROC::ci.auc(r)
  data.frame(Method = m, AUC = sprintf("%.3f (%.3f–%.3f)", ci[2], ci[1], ci[3]),
             Brier = round(brier(test$obese, methods[[m]]), 4))
}))
kable(meth_tab, caption = "Test-set comparison of classification methods")
save_tab(meth_tab, "week10_method_comparison")
```

## K-means clustering

K-means is **unsupervised**: it groups people by similarity in their characteristics without using obesity.
We use it in three ways: (a) to see whether natural age–diet profiles in the data line up with obesity,
(b) as a crude predictor (cluster membership) compared against the logistic model, and (c) to split the
logistic model's predicted risks into low/medium/high groups as a check of risk stratification.

```{r kmeans-k, fig.height=3.8}
# Continuous inputs only: K-means uses Euclidean distance, so a 3-level variable such as
# vitamin D would dominate the solution (clusters would just reproduce the vitamin D groups).
# Clusters are therefore "age-diet profiles"; vitamin D, diabetes and obesity are compared afterwards.
km_vars <- c("age", "SATPER1", "PEADDSD1", "energy_MJ")
Zall <- scale(d_pred[, km_vars])
k_try <- 2:8
wss <- sapply(k_try, function(k) kmeans(Zall, k, nstart = 25, iter.max = 50)$tot.withinss)
dmat <- dist(Zall)
sil <- sapply(k_try, function(k) {
  km <- kmeans(Zall, k, nstart = 25, iter.max = 50)
  mean(cluster::silhouette(km$cluster, dmat)[, "sil_width"])
})
k_opt <- k_try[which.max(sil)]
data.frame(k = k_try, WSS = wss, Silhouette = sil) %>%
  pivot_longer(-k) %>%
  ggplot(aes(k, value)) + geom_line() + geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(~name, scales = "free_y") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = k_opt, linetype = "dashed", colour = "firebrick") +
  labs(title = sprintf("Choosing k: elbow (WSS) and average silhouette — chosen k = %d", k_opt))
```

```{r kmeans-profile}
km <- kmeans(Zall, k_opt, nstart = 50, iter.max = 100)
d_pred$cluster <- factor(km$cluster)

prof <- d_pred %>% group_by(Cluster = cluster) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), `Mean age` = round(mean(age), 1),
            `Sat/trans fat %E` = round(mean(SATPER1), 1), `Added sugar %E` = round(mean(PEADDSD1), 1),
            `Energy MJ/day` = round(mean(energy_MJ), 1),
            `Vit D deficient %` = round(100 * mean(vitd_def == "Deficient"), 1),
            `Female %` = round(100 * mean(sex == "Female"), 1),
            `Diabetes %` = round(100 * mean(diabetes == "Diabetes"), 1),
            `Obese %` = round(100 * mean(obese), 1), .groups = "drop")
chi <- chisq.test(table(d_pred$cluster, d_pred$obese))
kable(prof, caption = sprintf("Cluster profiles (χ² test of obesity across clusters: p = %s; adjusted Rand index vs obesity = %.3f)",
                              fmt_p(chi$p.value), adj_rand(d_pred$cluster, d_pred$obese)))
save_tab(prof, "week10_kmeans_profiles")

pc <- prcomp(Zall)
data.frame(PC1 = pc$x[, 1], PC2 = pc$x[, 2], Cluster = d_pred$cluster, Obese = d_pred$obese_f) %>%
  ggplot(aes(PC1, PC2, colour = Cluster, shape = Obese)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) + scale_shape_manual(values = c(1, 17)) +
  labs(title = "K-means clusters on the first two principal components",
       subtitle = sprintf("PC1 + PC2 explain %.0f%% of variance",
                          100 * sum(pc$sdev[1:2]^2) / sum(pc$sdev^2)))
```

```{r kmeans-predict}
# (b) Cluster membership as a predictor: fit K-means on the TRAINING data only,
#     assign test cases to the nearest centroid, then compare test AUC with the logistic model.
mu_k <- colMeans(train[, km_vars]); sd_k <- apply(train[, km_vars], 2, sd)
Ztr_k <- scale(train[, km_vars], mu_k, sd_k); Zte_k <- scale(test[, km_vars], mu_k, sd_k)
km_tr <- kmeans(Ztr_k, k_opt, nstart = 50, iter.max = 100)
nearest <- function(Z, centers) apply(Z, 1, function(z) which.min(colSums((t(centers) - z)^2)))
train$cl <- factor(km_tr$cluster, levels = seq_len(k_opt))
test$cl  <- factor(nearest(Zte_k, km_tr$centers), levels = seq_len(k_opt))
cl_fit <- glm(obese ~ cl, data = train, family = binomial)
p_cl   <- predict(cl_fit, test, type = "response")

# (c) K-means on the model's predicted risk → three risk groups; observed obesity should rise across groups
risk_km <- kmeans(ho$P4_int$p, centers = 3, nstart = 25)
ord <- order(risk_km$centers)
risk_grp <- factor(match(risk_km$cluster, ord), 1:3, c("Low", "Medium", "High"))
risk_tab <- data.frame(group = risk_grp, y = test$obese, p = ho$P4_int$p) %>%
  group_by(`Risk group (K-means on predicted risk)` = group) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), `Mean predicted %` = round(100 * mean(p), 1),
            `Observed obese %` = round(100 * mean(y), 1), .groups = "drop")

kable(data.frame(Predictor = c("K-means cluster membership", "Logistic regression (P4_int)"),
                 `Test AUC` = round(c(as.numeric(pROC::auc(mk_roc(test$obese, p_cl))),
                                      as.numeric(pROC::auc(ho$P4_int$roc))), 3),
                 check.names = FALSE),
      caption = "Does unsupervised clustering predict obesity as well as the supervised model?")
kable(risk_tab, caption = "Risk stratification of the test set using K-means on predicted probabilities")
```

```{r summary-values, include=FALSE}
best_cv <- cv_sum$Model[1]
auc_m0  <- cv_sum$`CV AUC mean`[cv_sum$Model == "M0_AgeSex"]
auc_p4  <- cv_sum$`CV AUC mean`[cv_sum$Model == "P4_int"]

auc_word <- function(a) ifelse(a < 0.6, "poor", ifelse(a < 0.7, "modest", ifelse(a < 0.8, "acceptable", "good")))
```

**Week 9 – significance**

* **Vitamin D (Person 1):** adjusted `r or_txt(sw$P1_adj, "vitd3ModSevere")` for moderate/severe deficiency
  vs adequate; overall vitamin D effect `r sigtxt(p1_joint_a$p)` (joint p = `r fmt_p(p1_joint_a$p)`).
* **UPF proxy (Person 2):** adjusted `r or_txt(sw$P2_adj_full, "upf10")` per +10 %E (full sample).
* **Both (Person 3):** vitamin D `r or_txt(sw$P3_adj, "vitd3ModSevere")`; UPF `r or_txt(sw$P3_adj, "upf10")`.
* **Interaction (Person 4):** `r or_txt(sw$P4_int, int_term, "ratio of ORs")` — `r sigtxt(p4_wald$p)`
  (unweighted LRT p = `r fmt_p(p4_lrt[["Pr(>Chi)"]][2])`).
* Lowest AIC: **`r w9$Model[which.min(w9$AIC)]`**.

**Week 10 – prediction**

* Best cross-validated model: **`r best_cv`**. Age + sex alone gave CV AUC = `r auc_m0`; the full model gave
  CV AUC = `r auc_p4` (*`r auc_word(auc_p4)`* discrimination). The exposures are associated with obesity at the
  population level, but `r ifelse(auc_p4 < 0.7, "they are weak tools for predicting whether an individual is obese", "they also discriminate reasonably between individuals")`.
* Accuracy at a 0.5 threshold is close to the no-information rate (`r round(1 - mean(test$obese), 3)`) because
  obesity is the minority class; this is why threshold-free metrics (AUC, Brier) and a Youden threshold are reported.
* Calibration of the full model: Hosmer–Lemeshow p = `r fmt_p(hl[3])`, slope = `r round(coef(cal_fit)[2], 2)`.
* K-means (k = `r k_opt`) produced clusters with obesity prevalence ranging from
  `r min(prof$"Obese %")`% to `r max(prof$"Obese %")`% (χ² p = `r fmt_p(chi$p.value)`), but cluster membership
  gave a test AUC of `r round(auc_cl, 3)` versus `r round(auc_lg, 3)` for the logistic model`r ifelse(auc_cl < auc_lg, ", as expected for a method that never sees the outcome", "")`.

**Limitations to discuss:** cross-sectional data (reverse causation, especially obesity → low vitamin D); the UPF proxy
is nutrient-based and from a single 24-hour recall; only `r sum(d_bio$diabetes == "Diabetes")` participants with
diabetes (low power for the interaction); complete-case analysis restricted to biomedical participants; the
full-sample design has no replicate weights, so its SEs may be slightly underestimated.
